categories.yc-backstory: YC backstory / How To Build The Future

contexts.not-a-founder: builder who does not see themselves as a founder
contexts.where-to-start: does not know where to start
contexts.first-time-full-picture: first-time founder, needs the full picture

pool.title: My $200 million startup mistake: Peter Thiel asked and I said no
pool.blurb: The single best "why you should take the leap" video. Peter Thiel writes him a check at dinner, he says no because he might get promoted to Level 60. That 1% stake would be worth $350-500M today.

pool.title: Unconventional Advice for Founders
pool.blurb: The magnum opus. Covers everything a pre-launch founder needs: get therapy before your psychology kills your company, good ideas look like bad ideas, the Katamari Damacy metaphor for growth. No filler.

pool.title: The New Way To Build A Startup
pool.blurb: The 2026 playbook. Introduces the "20x company" - tiny teams beating incumbents through AI automation. Three real case studies. If you are starting something now and are not thinking this way, you are already behind.

pool.title: How To Build The Future: Sam Altman
pool.blurb: Sam talks about what it takes to go from an idea to something real: picking what is important, finding your tribe, and why conviction matters more than credentials.

pool.title: What Founders Can Do To Improve Their Design Game
pool.blurb: Garry was a designer before he was an investor. Taste and craft are the real competitive advantage, not MBA skills or fundraising tricks.

pool.title: Tom Blomfield: How I Created Two Billion-Dollar Fintech Startups
pool.blurb: Tom built Monzo from nothing into a bank used by 10% of the UK. The actual human journey: fear, mess, persistence. Makes founding feel like something a real person does.

pool.title: DoorDash CEO: Customer Obsession, Surviving Startup Death & Creating A New Market
pool.blurb: Tony started DoorDash by literally driving food deliveries himself. If you have ever thought "I am not the startup type," this will change your mind.

pool.title: How to Spend Your 20s in the AI Era
pool.blurb: The old playbook (good job, climb the ladder) may not be the best path anymore. How to position yourself to build things that matter in an AI-first world.

pool.title: How Do Billion Dollar Startups Start?
pool.blurb: They start tiny, scrappy, and embarrassing. Demystifies the origin stories and shows that the beginning always looks like a side project, not a corporation.

pool.title: Billion-Dollar Unpopular Startup Ideas
pool.blurb: Uber, Coinbase, DoorDash all sounded terrible at first. The best opportunities are the ones most people dismiss. Liberating if your idea feels weird.

pool.title: Vertical AI Agents Could Be 10X Bigger Than SaaS
pool.blurb: The most-watched Lightcone episode. If you are building in AI, this is the landscape map: where the biggest opportunities are and why vertical agents win.

pool.title: The Truth About Building AI Startups Today
pool.blurb: Cuts through the hype. What is actually working, what is not, and where the real defensibility comes from in AI startups right now.

pool.title: Startup Ideas You Can Now Build With AI
pool.blurb: Concrete, actionable ideas for things that were not possible 12 months ago. If you are looking for what to build, start here.

pool.title: Vibe Coding Is The Future
pool.blurb: Building software just changed forever. If you can describe what you want, you can build it. The barrier to being a technical founder has never been lower.

pool.title: How To Get AI Startup Ideas
pool.blurb: Not theoretical. Walks through specific AI startup ideas that are working right now and explains why the window is open.

pool.title: 10 People + AI = Billion Dollar Company?
pool.blurb: The thesis behind the 20x company. Small teams with AI leverage are outperforming 100-person incumbents. If you are a solo builder or small team, this is your permission slip to think big.

pool.title: Should You Start A Startup?
pool.blurb: Directly addresses the question most people are too afraid to ask out loud. Breaks down the real tradeoffs honestly, without hype.

pool.title: How to Get and Evaluate Startup Ideas
pool.blurb: YC's most-watched Startup School video. How founders actually stumbled into their ideas by paying attention to problems in their own lives.

pool.title: How David Lieb Turned a Failing Startup Into Google Photos
pool.blurb: His company Bump was dying. He noticed a photo-sharing behavior in his own data, and it became Google Photos (1B+ users). A masterclass in seeing opportunity where others see failure.

pool.title: Tips For Technical Startup Founders
pool.blurb: How to leverage your engineering skills as a founder rather than thinking you need to become a different person.

pool.title: Why Startup Founders Should Launch Companies Sooner Than They Think
pool.blurb: Most builders over-prepare and under-ship. If your instinct is "it is not ready yet," this will push you to put it in front of people now.

pool.title: How To Talk To Users
pool.blurb: You do not need sales skills. You need genuine conversations about problems. The most approachable tactical talk for someone who has never done it.

pool.title: How To Find A Co-Founder
pool.blurb: The practical mechanics of finding someone to build with. If "I do not want to do this alone" is stopping you, this removes that blocker.

pool.title: Should You Quit Your Job At A Unicorn?
pool.blurb: Directly speaks to people at big tech companies who feel the pull to build something of their own. If that is your situation, this is the permission slip.

pool.title: How to Do Great Work
pool.blurb: Not about startups. About finding the most meaningful work of your life. The roadmap that often leads to founding without ever saying "startup."

pool.title: How to Do What You Love
pool.blurb: Most people keep their real interests separate from their career. Makes the case for collapsing that gap, which is usually how companies get born.

pool.title: The Bus Ticket Theory of Genius
pool.blurb: The thing you are obsessively into that other people find boring? PG argues it is the actual mechanism behind every breakthrough.

pool.title: Why to Not Not Start a Startup
pool.blurb: Takes apart every quiet reason you have for not starting (too young, no idea, do not know business) and shows why none hold up.

pool.title: Before the Startup
pool.blurb: Written specifically for people who have not started anything yet. What to focus on now, what to ignore, and how to tell if this path is for you.

pool.title: Superlinear Returns
pool.blurb: Some efforts compound exponentially; most do not. Why channeling your builder skills into the right project has a payoff structure a normal career cannot match.

pool.title: How to Get Startup Ideas
pool.blurb: The best ideas are not brainstormed. They are noticed. Teaches you to look at your own frustrations and recognize which ones could be companies.

pool.title: Schlep Blindness
pool.blurb: The best opportunities hide inside boring, tedious problems everyone avoids. If you are willing to tackle the unsexy thing you see up close, you might already be standing on a company.

pool.title: You Weren't Meant to Have a Boss
pool.blurb: If working inside a big organization has always felt slightly wrong, this explains why. Small groups on self-chosen problems is the natural state for builders.

pool.title: Relentlessly Resourceful
pool.blurb: PG's two-word description of the ideal founder. Not brilliant. Not visionary. Just someone who keeps figuring things out. If that is you, you are already qualified.
